html:
Banská Štiavnica is a mining town in central Slovakia that got town rights around 1238 and became one of the richest sources of silver in medieval Europe. With nearby Kremnica, famed for its gold and its mint, it made the mountains of Upper Hungary a treasury for the crown.

German miners settled here at the invitation of Hungarian kings. Kremnica struck gold florins from 1328. In 1627 Banská Štiavnica's miners were among the first in Europe to use gunpowder in a mine. In 1762 Maria Theresa founded a mining academy here, one of the first technical colleges in the world. The old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
